def index_moves(pkg, part):
    """The part's cost drivers with each index's change over the last 12 months."""
    out = []
    for d in rows(pkg, "SELECT series_id, weight FROM cost_drivers WHERE part_id = ?", (part,)):
        sql = "SELECT value FROM index_values WHERE series_id = ? ORDER BY month DESC"
        v = rows(pkg, sql, (d["series_id"],), 13)
        if len(v) == 13 and v[12]["value"]:
            d["change_12m_pct"] = round((v[0]["value"] / v[12]["value"] - 1) * 100, 1)
        out.append(d)
    return out


def about(pkg, sid, prefix):
    """[(id, row)] of this supplier under an ID prefix, latest first, from the ID index: the Sunday
    release reaches it, the SQL tables do not."""
    found = [(ref, pkg.lookup(ref) or {}) for ref in pkg.ids(prefix)]
    return sorted((f for f in found if f[1].get("supplier") == sid), key=lambda f: str(f[1].get("date")), reverse=True)


def letters(pkg, sid):
    """Its latest letters and our notes on it, without the routine mail."""
    out = []
    for ref, d in safe_rows(about, pkg, sid, "doc:"):
        if any(n in (d.get("title") or "").lower() for n in NOISE) or len(out) >= 6:
            continue
        try:
            out.append(f"{d.get('date')} {d.get('type')}: {pkg.document(ref)[:700]}")
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - a row without a readable file
            out.append(f"{d.get('date')} {d.get('type')}: {d.get('title')}")
    return out


def news(pkg, sid, limit=5):
    """The latest news about it, text included."""
    out = []
    for ref, d in safe_rows(about, pkg, sid, "news:")[:limit]:
        try:
            body = pkg.document(ref)[:500]
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - a row without a readable text: its headline still counts
            body = ""
        out.append(f"{d.get('date')}: {d.get('headline')}. {body}".strip())
    return out


def safe_rows(fn, *args):
    try:
        return fn(*args)
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - a package without an ID index: the analyst sees less
        return []


def digest(pkg, case, sid, group):
    """The data one specialist studies, as text; empty when the package knows nothing here."""
    parts = case.get("parts") or []
    part = parts[0] if parts else None
    keys = {"part": (part,), "sid": (sid,), "part_sid": (part, sid), "doc": (case.get("trigger_doc"),)}
    out = [block(title, rows(pkg, sql, keys[key], limit)) for title, sql, key, limit in TABLES[group]]
    if group == "economics":
        out.append(block("COST DRIVERS OF THE PART (weight, index change over 12 months in %)", index_moves(pkg, part)))
    if group == "persona":
        out.append(block("NEWS", news(pkg, sid)))
        out.append(block("LETTERS AND NOTES", letters(pkg, sid)))
    return "\n".join(filter(None, out))


def clamp(raw, case):
    """The lead's strategy with every value from the case or from its list; junk is dropped."""
    options = case.get("term_options") or {}
    trades = []
    for t in raw.get("trades") if isinstance(raw.get("trades"), list) else []:
        field = t.get("field") if isinstance(t, dict) else None
        if field in case.get("negotiable", []) and field != "unit_price" and t.get("value") in options.get(field, []):
            trades.append({"field": field, "value": t["value"], "why": " ".join(str(t.get("why") or "").split())[:160]})
    order = raw.get("claim_order")
    return {
        "trades": trades[:TRADES],
        "claim_order": [k for k in order if k in CLAIM_KINDS] if isinstance(order, list) else [],
        "tone": raw.get("tone") if raw.get("tone") in ("warm", "businesslike") else None,
        "notes": " ".join(str(raw.get("notes") or "").split())[:600],
        "reason": str(raw.get("reason") or "")[:300],
    }


def briefs(case, pkg, complete, budget_s=BUDGET_S):
    """{supplier_id: brief} for a case: the specialists' findings, the lead's checked strategy and
    the demo bidding's playbook. {} without a model; a supplier whose lead was late has no brief."""
    if complete is None:
        return {}
    if case["case_id"] in CACHE:
        return CACHE[case["case_id"]]
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    end = t0 + budget_s
    head = case_brief(case)
    suppliers = case.get("suppliers") or []
    known = pkg is not None and any(pkg.lookup(r) for r in case.get("refs") or [])
    jobs = {}
    for sid in suppliers:
        for group, (scope, goal) in GROUPS.items():
            data = digest(pkg, case, sid, group) if known else ""
            if data:
                system = SPECIALIST.format(name=group, scope=scope, goal=goal)
                jobs[sid, group] = llm.submit(complete, system, f"{head}\n\nSUPPLIER {sid}\n{data}")
    stage = min(end, time.monotonic() + STAGE_S)
    found = {key: llm.read_json(f, stage - time.monotonic()) for key, f in jobs.items()}
    lessons = memory.recall(case)
    second = {}
    for sid in suppliers:
        findings = {g: (found.get((sid, g)) or {}) for g in GROUPS}
        report = "\n".join(
            f"{g.upper()} (leverage: {f.get('leverage', 'unknown')}): "
            + " ".join(str(x) for x in f.get("findings") or [])
            for g, f in findings.items()
            if f.get("findings")
        )
        user = "\n\n".join(
            filter(
                None,
                [
                    head,
                    f"SUPPLIER {sid}, one of {len(suppliers)} in this case",
                    block("ANALYSTS", [report or NO_DATA]),
                    block("EARLIER NEGOTIATIONS OF THIS KIND (one run each: observations, not rules)", lessons),
                ],
            )
        )
        second[sid] = (findings, user, llm.submit(complete, LEAD, user), llm.submit(complete, rehearsal.SUPPLIER, user))
    stage = min(end, time.monotonic() + STAGE_S)
    third = {}
    for sid, (findings, user, lead, supplier) in second.items():
        strategy = llm.read_json(lead, stage - time.monotonic())
        view = rehearsal.supplier_view(llm.read_json(supplier, stage - time.monotonic()))
        buyer = None
        if view["arguments"]:  # the demo bidding's second half: our side answers its arguments
            buyer = llm.submit(complete, rehearsal.BUYER, f"{user}\n\n{rehearsal.exchange(view)}")
        third[sid] = (findings, strategy, view, buyer)
    stage = min(end, time.monotonic() + STAGE_S)
    out = {}
    for sid, (findings, strategy, view, buyer) in third.items():
        if strategy is None:
            continue
        checked = clamp(strategy, case)
        if not any(findings.values()):
            checked["trades"] = []  # a trade for a supplier we know nothing about is a guess
        out[sid] = {
            **checked,
            "playbook": rehearsal.playbook(
                view, llm.read_json(buyer, stage - time.monotonic()), any(findings.values())
            ),
            "findings": {g: f.get("findings") for g, f in findings.items() if f.get("findings")},
        }
    log.info("%s research in %.1fs: %s", case["case_id"], time.monotonic() - t0, json.dumps(out, ensure_ascii=False))
    CACHE[case["case_id"]] = out
    return out

"""The live analyst: reads each supplier e-mail as it arrives (the opening quote included) and
tells the bidder the mood of the person writing and the tactic for our next move, so the bidding
follows the supplier we actually meet and not only the one in our files. It also matches the
e-mail to the arguments the demo bidding expected, so the writer gets our prepared answer.
Everything it returns comes from a fixed list; the policy decides what each value changes. Traits
that move anchors or rates stay with the patterns in `personas.py`: a model's guess there costs too
much."""

from . import llm

TIMEOUT_S = 6.0
MOODS = ("warm", "neutral", "irritated", "pressured")
TACTICS = ("steady", "hold", "argue")
ASKS = ("volume", "proof", "payment", "target")  # the kinds `policy.asks` reads

SYSTEM = """You are the analyst next to our buyer at Hollerau Pumpenwerke during a negotiation. Read
the supplier's latest e-mail and say who we are dealing with right now and what to do next.
Return JSON only:
{"mood": the mood of the person writing: "warm", "neutral", "irritated" or "pressured",
 "tactic": our best next move, one of:
   "hold" - it still concedes or signals room to move: we move less than usual,
   "argue" - it brings an argument we can answer or doubts our data: we answer it with evidence,
   "steady" - none of these,
 "argument": the number of the EXPECTED ARGUMENT its e-mail makes, or 0 if none,
 "asks": what it asks of us, from this list only: volume, proof, payment, target,
 "notes": one or two sentences for the colleague who writes our reply: what this person cares
  about right now and how to answer them. No figures, no dates.}"""


def read(complete, case, body, ours, theirs, arguments=(), timeout=TIMEOUT_S):
    """{mood, tactic, argument, asks, notes} for a supplier e-mail, every value from its list; None
    when the model is off, late or wrong. `ours`, `theirs`: the price paths so far; `arguments`:
    what the demo bidding expected this supplier to say (`argument` indexes them from 1)."""
    expected = "\n".join(f"{i}. {a}" for i, a in enumerate(arguments, 1)) or "none prepared"
    user = (
        f"CASE: {case.get('title')} ({case.get('type')}, goal {case['buyer'].get('category_goal')})\n"
        f"OUR PRICES SO FAR: {ours}\nITS PRICES SO FAR: {theirs}\nEXPECTED ARGUMENTS:\n{expected}\n"
        f"ITS E-MAIL:\n{(body or '')[:2500]}"
    )
    raw = llm.ask_json(complete, SYSTEM, user, min(timeout, TIMEOUT_S))
    if raw is None:
        return None
    asks = raw.get("asks")
    argument = raw.get("argument")
    return {
        "mood": raw.get("mood") if raw.get("mood") in MOODS else "neutral",
        "tactic": raw.get("tactic") if raw.get("tactic") in TACTICS else "steady",
        "argument": argument if isinstance(argument, int) and 0 < argument <= len(arguments) else 0,
        "asks": [a for a in asks if a in ASKS] if isinstance(asks, list) else [],
        "notes": " ".join(str(raw.get("notes") or "").split())[:400],
    }

"""The demo bidding before the real one: a supplier subagent and a buyer subagent argue the case
against each other. The supplier, in character and knowing what our analysts found, says which
arguments it will bring, which weak points it hopes we miss and what it would give price for. The
buyer answers each argument and picks the weak points to press. What comes out is a playbook for
the real bidding: the live analyst matches a supplier e-mail to one of the expected arguments and
the writer gets our prepared answer. Words only: every price and term stays with code, and a line
with a figure in it is dropped (the writer may not use one)."""

import re

SUPPLIER = """You play the sales lead of a supplier in a rehearsal of a negotiation with your customer
Hollerau Pumpenwerke. Below is the case and what the customer's analysts found out about your
company. Stay in character and be honest with yourself: this rehearsal is private.
Return JSON only:
{"arguments": the up to 4 arguments you will bring to defend your price or refuse a request, one
  sentence each, strongest first,
 "weak_points": the up to 3 points in your position you hope the customer does not raise, one
  sentence each,
 "wants": the up to 3 things other than price you would give a better price for, one short phrase each}
Write no figures, dates or names."""

BUYER = """You are the senior buyer of Hollerau Pumpenwerke in a rehearsal of a negotiation. Below is
the case, what our analysts found, and what the supplier's sales lead said in the rehearsal: the
arguments it will bring and the weak points it hopes we miss.
Find our best answer to each of its arguments: reasoning that is fair, factual and hard to
dismiss. An answer may acknowledge its point, put it in proportion and point to what the case and
our analysts' findings show we already bring, and to nothing else. An answer never promises or offers
anything new, sets no condition, and is never a threat, a deadline, a bluff or a request for its
cost breakdown (all tested, none works).
Return JSON only:
{"rebuttals": one object per supplier argument, {"to": the argument's number, "answer": our answer
  in one or two sentences},
 "press": the up to 2 weak points worth raising, each as one polite, respectful sentence we could
  write, taken only from what the analysts found, never about its finances; [] when the analysts
  found nothing}
Write no figures, dates or names: code adds the data."""

DIGIT = re.compile(r"\d")


def lines(value, limit, chars=260):
    """A subagent's list as clean sentences: strings only, no figures, capped in number and length."""
    out = []
    for item in value if isinstance(value, list) else []:
        text = " ".join(str(item).split())[:chars] if isinstance(item, str) else ""
        if text and not DIGIT.search(text):
            out.append(text)
    return out[:limit]


def supplier_view(raw):
    """What the supplier subagent said, clamped."""
    raw = raw or {}
    return {
        "arguments": lines(raw.get("arguments"), 4),
        "weak_points": lines(raw.get("weak_points"), 3),
        "wants": lines(raw.get("wants"), 3, 80),
    }


def exchange(view):
    """The supplier's side of the rehearsal as the buyer subagent reads it."""
    numbered = "\n".join(f"{i}. {a}" for i, a in enumerate(view["arguments"], 1))
    weak = "\n".join(f"- {w}" for w in view["weak_points"])
    return f"THE SUPPLIER'S ARGUMENTS:\n{numbered}\nWEAK POINTS IT HOPES WE MISS:\n{weak or '- none named'}"


def playbook(view, raw, informed=True):
    """The rehearsal's result: each expected argument with our answer ("" when the buyer found
    none), the weak points to press and what the supplier wants besides price. `informed`: our
    analysts had data on this supplier; without it a "weak point" is a guess, and we never write
    a supplier something our records do not show."""
    raw = raw or {}
    answers = {}
    for r in raw.get("rebuttals") if isinstance(raw.get("rebuttals"), list) else []:
        if isinstance(r, dict) and isinstance(r.get("to"), int) and lines([r.get("answer")], 1, 400):
            answers[r["to"]] = lines([r["answer"]], 1, 400)[0]
    return {
        "arguments": view["arguments"],
        "rebuttals": [answers.get(i, "") for i in range(1, len(view["arguments"]) + 1)],
        "press": lines(raw.get("press"), 2) if informed else [],
        "wants": view["wants"],
    }

"""The negotiation policy, per supplier thread: plan the non-price terms by C at the supplier's
own valuation, open below its quote, then move toward its counter round by round so it keeps
conceding, with verified claims spread over the rounds. Close on its final offer, its agreement or
the round limit; in relationship goals stop at the price where C is lowest.

What the suppliers showed (sandbox and practice, `docs/learnings.md`):
- they concede only after a move from us and agree as soon as our sheet reaches the counter they
  would make, so our sheet stays below their counter until the end;
- every verified claim they take into account lowers where they stop, most of it in round 1;
- patience runs out at a cumulative gap of about 40 % between our sheets and their counters
  (summed per round, relative to their price), much earlier for a supplier selling near its cost
  or one that is fully booked: a final offer, or a walk-away;
- a large first concession means a deep floor: then we hold low instead of meeting it."""

import base64
import functools
import json
import logging
import re
import time

from arena_kit.docs import standard_terms
from arena_kit.play import ENDED, latest, live_threads, moves_left, standing

from . import analyst, llm, writer

FRACTION = 0.3  # share of the gap to the supplier's counter we move per round
# Opening price as a share of its quote at our terms, by category goal. Practice C_best sat 12 to
# 22 % below the quote in leverage, routine and secure-supply cases, 1.5 to 3 % in stabilise ones.
ANCHOR = {"leverage": 0.78, "routine": 0.82, "secure_supply": 0.88, "quality_first": 0.88, "stabilise": 0.92}
ANCHOR_MIN = 0.75  # never open lower than this share (an insult costs patience)
BUDGET = 1.0  # patience: the cumulative relative gap we show (no cap for a typical supplier)
DEEP = 0.06  # a first concession this large (share of its quote) means a deep floor
MIN_MOVE = 0.002  # every sheet moves at least this share of the price
FIRST_CLAIMS, LATER_CLAIMS = 3, 1
HOLD = 0.7  # the live analyst's "hold": it still concedes, we move this share of our usual step
ANALYST_MIN_S = 10.0  # the clocks must leave this much for analyst and writer together, else no analyst
TRADE_MIN = 0.7  # a trade sheet's price never sits below this share of what the supplier quotes for it
DONE = {"agreed", "final_offer"}

# What the supplier's e-mail asks of us
ASKS = {
    # a binding volume figure; stated in words with the figure, it was "taken into account" (D01, D02)
    "volume": r"volume (can )?you (can )?commit|binding (higher )?volume|higher (order )?volume|volume figures"
    r"|confirm .{0,40}volume|anticipated (order )?volume",
    # proof of the forecast or of figures we mentioned without an ID
    "proof": r"proof of|send us the data|figures is that based|provide the (volume|forecast|binding)"
    r"|forecast data|volume data",
    # it wants to be paid sooner
    "payment": r"faster payment|pay(ment)? (terms )?(earlier|faster|sooner|within)|need .{0,12}days payment"
    r"|shorter payment|quicker payment|cash flow",
    # it asks for our current price level or our target
    "target": r"what price|which price|your target|price you have in mind",
}


def asks(body):
    """The kinds of ask in a supplier e-mail, in a fixed order. The bots write their asks in a few
    fixed sentences ("Which volume can you commit to?", "Please send us the data."), so plain
    patterns read them; no model, no latency."""
    text = body or ""
    return [k for k, pat in ASKS.items() if re.search(pat, text, re.I)]


class Side:
    """One supplier thread: what we know and what we did."""

    def __init__(self, sid):
        self.sid = sid
        self.std = {}
        self.prof = {}
        self.est = {}
        self.terms = {}  # our planned non-price terms (with a price placeholder)
        self.quote = None  # its opening price at our terms
        self.last_sheet = {}  # its previous standing terms
        self.late = 0  # our messages the arena counted as rounds although they came too late
        self.anchor = None
        self.target = None  # relationship goals: the price with the lowest C
        self.budget = BUDGET
        self.claims = []
        self.ours = []  # our prices at s.terms, one per message with a sheet
        self.theirs = []  # its price at our terms, one per reply
        self.gaps = []  # relative gap of each of our sheets to its counter
        self.state = "open"  # open | mirror | done | ended
        self.prev_state = "open"  # the state before the message in flight
        self.pending = None  # the message in flight: what to undo if it times out
        self.last_sent_terms = None  # last committed primary sheet, for the no-progress guard
        self.used_claim_families = set()  # semantic evidence already used with this supplier
        self.offered_trade_keys = set()  # term/value alternatives already offered in this thread
        self.term_change = False  # its last counter changed our non-price terms
        self.last_reply = None
        self.asks = []  # what its last e-mail asked of us (asks)
        self.attached = set()  # files we already sent it
        self.research = ""  # the lead researcher's notes for the e-mail writer
        self.trades = []  # terms the lead expects it to value: offered next to our opening sheet
        self.active_trades = []  # explicit supplier needs priced for the current move
        self.playbook = {}  # the demo bidding: its expected arguments, our answers, points to press
        self.live = ""  # the live analyst's notes on its last e-mail
        self.mood = None  # the live analyst on its last e-mail: the writer's mood
        self.tactic = None  # and our next move: steady | hold | argue
        self.tactics = []  # every tactic played, for the debrief
        self.argument = 0  # which expected argument its last e-mail made (1-based), 0 for none


class Negotiator:
    def __init__(self, case, pkg=None, complete=None, briefs=None):
        """`briefs`: the research team's brief per supplier (`research.briefs`); None plays the
        plain price engine, without the research strategy and without the live analyst."""
        self.case, self.pkg, self.complete, self.briefs = case, pkg, complete, briefs
        self.bank = ClaimBank(pkg, case)
        self.sides = {}
        self.used = set()  # claim IDs cited in this case (a rival quote: per supplier)
        self.notes = []  # what we decided, for the log
        self.writer_s = llm.TIMEOUT_S  # wall clock the model may take on the move being built

    # -- setup -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def setup(self, sid, events):
        case, s = self.case, Side(sid)
        s.std = safe(lambda: standard_terms(events), {}) or {}
        sheet_id, quote = standing(events)
        s.prof = safe(lambda: profile(self.pkg, sid), profile(None, sid))
        self.read_signals(s, latest(events).get("body"))
        brief = (self.briefs or {}).get(sid) or {}
        self.sides[sid] = s
        if not sheet_id or quote.get("unit_price") is None:
            s.state = "ended"
            return s
        s.last_sheet = quote
        # a bundle's should-cost is unknown: one component's cost is not the price unit of the kit
        parts = case.get("parts") or []
        full_cost, own_plant = (
            safe(lambda: self.full_cost(parts[0], sid), (None, False)) if len(parts) == 1 else (None, False)
        )
        lead = quote.get("lead_time_days") or s.std.get("lead_time_days")
        overtime = 0.005 if "capacity_full" in s.prof["signals"] else 0.001
        s.est = eco.estimate(
            case, s.std or quote, s.prof["rate"], full_cost, safe(lambda: self.real_ppm(sid)), lead, overtime
        )
        q_price = quote["unit_price"]
        goal, signals = case["buyer"].get("category_goal"), s.prof["signals"]
        sustainable = case["buyer"].get("sustainable_margin_pct") or 0
        if full_cost and goal in eco.RELATIONSHIP_GOALS:
            # it quoted with its margin: a should-cost above that is our estimate's error (P02: 374.95
            # against a quote of 370.96; the relationship charge of the deals says about 368)
            full_cost = min(full_cost, eco.value(case, quote, s.est) * (1 - sustainable / 100))
            s.est["full_cost"] = full_cost
        ratio = ANCHOR.get(goal, 0.85)
        near_cost = bool(own_plant and full_cost >= 0.98 * q_price)  # it sells at our cost estimate
        if goal in eco.RELATIONSHIP_GOALS:
            s.budget = 0.3
        if "price_frozen" in signals:
            ratio = max(ratio, 0.95)  # its list price does not move far; a deep cut only costs patience
        if "capacity_full" in signals:
            ratio, s.budget = max(ratio, 0.93), min(s.budget, 0.16)
        if near_cost:
            ratio, s.budget = max(ratio, 0.97), min(s.budget, 0.14)
        current = case["buyer"].get("current_unit_price")
        if case.get("type") == "price_increase" and current:
            ratio = min(ratio, current / q_price)  # a price increase opens at today's price at most
        ratio = max(ANCHOR_MIN, ratio)
        if brief:
            self.apply(s, brief)
        # terms planned at the price we open with: coverage pays off at a low price, not at the quote
        planned = safe(lambda: eco.plan_terms(case, s.std, s.est, quote, q_price * ratio))
        s.terms = planned[0] if planned else eco.complete_offer(case, eco.at_price(quote, q_price * ratio))
        s.anchor = s.terms["unit_price"]
        s.quote = safe(
            lambda: round(eco.price_for_value(case, s.terms, s.est, eco.value(case, quote, s.est)), 2), q_price
        )
        if full_cost:
            # also for a supplier selling at our cost estimate: below the optimum a lower price costs
            # us more than it saves, and pushing on made Nordmark withdraw (P02 v1)
            s.target = safe(lambda: eco.relationship_optimum(case, s.terms, s.std, s.est, full_cost * 0.85, s.quote))
        safe(lambda: self.trade_clause(s, quote, full_cost))
        s.claims = safe(lambda: self.bank.for_supplier(sid, q_price), [])
        order = brief.get("claim_order") or []  # the arguments the lead expects this supplier to accept, first
        s.claims.sort(key=lambda c: order.index(c["kind"]) if c["kind"] in order else len(order))
        self.note(
            sid,
            "setup",
            quote=quote,
            std=s.std,
            profile=s.prof,
            full_cost=full_cost,
            near_cost=near_cost,
            terms=s.terms,
            quote_at_terms=s.quote,
            anchor=s.anchor,
            target=s.target,
            budget=s.budget,
            claims=[c["text"] for c in s.claims],
        )
        return s

    def apply(self, s, brief):
        """The research team's brief on this thread: the lead's trades wait for our opening sheet,
        the demo bidding's playbook for the supplier's arguments; notes and tone go to the e-mail
        writer. Prices and pace stay with the policy: a model moving them cost score (D01, D02,
        P04, `docs/learnings.md`)."""
        s.research = brief.get("notes") or ""
        s.trades = brief.get("trades") or []
        s.playbook = brief.get("playbook") or {}
        if brief.get("tone"):
            s.prof["warm"] = brief["tone"] == "warm"
        self.note(
            s.sid,
            "research",
            trades=s.trades,
            reason=brief.get("reason"),
            playbook=s.playbook,
            findings=brief.get("findings"),
        )

    def trade_sheets(self, s, main):
        """The lead's trades as extra sheets next to our opening sheet `main`: each changes one
        term and carries the price at which it costs us exactly what `main` costs, so whichever
        the supplier picks, we lose nothing and learn what it values. A trade whose price would
        sit at or above what the supplier quotes for those terms, or far below it, is not offered."""
        case, out = self.case, []
        c_main = eco.cost(case, main, s.std, s.est)
        for trade in s.trades:
            terms = {**main, trade["field"]: trade["value"]}
            if terms == main or not eco.must_haves_ok(case, terms, s.std):
                continue
            lo, hi = 0.0, main["unit_price"] * 3
            if (
                not eco.cost(case, eco.at_price(terms, lo), s.std, s.est)
                < c_main
                < eco.cost(case, eco.at_price(terms, hi), s.std, s.est)
            ):
                continue
            for _ in range(50):  # C rises with the price
                mid = (lo + hi) / 2
                lo, hi = (mid, hi) if eco.cost(case, eco.at_price(terms, mid), s.std, s.est) < c_main else (lo, mid)
            sheet = eco.at_price(terms, int(lo * 100) / 100)
            quoted = eco.price_for_value(case, terms, s.est, eco.value(case, eco.at_price(s.terms, s.quote), s.est))
            if not TRADE_MIN * quoted <= sheet["unit_price"] < 0.995 * quoted:
                continue
            out.append(sheet)
            self.note(s.sid, "trade_sheet", trade=trade, price=sheet["unit_price"], quoted=round(quoted, 2))
        return out

    def trade_clause(self, s, quote, full_cost):
        """An index clause the supplier values more than it costs us (its driver rose over the
        year, the case's path is small): offer it from the start at the price worth the same to it
        as our anchor without it, and in a relationship goal no lower than the relationship
        optimum, where it is agreed at once (P02: Nordmark agreed to a 5 % copper deadband 4 %
        below its fixed price). No trade where its value equals our cost (P08, P18)."""
        case = self.case
        if "index_clause" not in case["negotiable"] or quote.get("index_clause"):
            return
        if "hedged" in s.prof["signals"]:
            return  # its material is bought forward at fixed prices: the index does not reach its costs
        for clause in case.get("term_options", {}).get("index_clause") or []:
            if clause and clause.get("series") not in s.est["index_moves"]:
                move = self.bank.move12(clause["series"])
                if move is not None:
                    s.est["index_moves"][clause["series"]] = move
        clause = eco.clause_trade(case, s.est)
        if not clause or s.terms.get("index_clause") == clause:
            return
        target_value = eco.value(case, s.terms, s.est)  # our anchor as it is worth to the supplier
        terms = {**s.terms, "index_clause": clause}
        price = eco.price_for_value(case, terms, s.est, target_value)
        floor = None
        if full_cost and case["buyer"].get("category_goal") in eco.RELATIONSHIP_GOALS:
            floor = eco.relationship_optimum(case, terms, s.std, s.est, full_cost * 0.85, s.quote)
            price = max(price, floor or 0.0)
        if not eco.must_haves_ok(case, eco.at_price(terms, price), s.std):
            return
        s.terms = eco.at_price(terms, price)
        s.anchor = s.terms["unit_price"]
        s.target = floor or s.target
        self.note(s.sid, "clause_trade", clause=clause, anchor=s.anchor, target=s.target)

    def full_cost(self, part, sid):
        """(should-cost of the part, whether it models this supplier's own plant): full cost
        without margin. A generic estimate (a German cost base) says little about one supplier."""
        rows = self.bank.query("SELECT id, supplier_id, unit_cost FROM should_cost WHERE part_id = ?", (part,))
        own = [r for r in rows if r.get("supplier_id") == sid]
        if own:
            return own[0]["unit_cost"], True
        generic = [r for r in rows if not r.get("supplier_id")]
        if generic:
            return generic[0]["unit_cost"], False
        for ref in self.bank.ids("cost:"):  # the case's own facts (no table rows)
            f = self.bank.fact(ref)
            if f and f.get("part") == part and f.get("unit_cost"):
                return f["unit_cost"], f.get("supplier") == sid
        return None, False

    def real_ppm(self, sid):
        """The defect rate it really delivers (latest scorecard), what a chargeback costs it."""
        ids = self.bank.ids(f"sc:{sid.split(':')[-1]}@")
        f = self.bank.fact(ids[-1]) if ids else None
        return f.get("ppm") if f else None

    def restore(self, sid, events):
        """A resumed session (a crash, a restart): rebuild what we sent and what it answered from
        the thread, so the next move continues the path instead of opening at the anchor again."""
        s = self.sides[sid]
        ours = [m for m in events if m.get("from") == "buyer" and m.get("term_sheets")]
        if s.state == "ended" or not ours:
            return
        s.terms = eco.complete_offer(self.case, ours[-1]["term_sheets"][0]["terms"])
        theirs = None
        for m in events:
            if m.get("from") == "buyer":
                refs = m.get("refs") or []
                self.used.update(refs)
                s.used_claim_families.update(
                    family for ref in refs for family in self.claim_families({"kind": "forecast", "ids": [ref]})
                )
                if m.get("term_sheets"):
                    sent_sheets = [sh.get("terms") or {} for sh in m["term_sheets"]]
                    s.last_sent_terms = dict(sent_sheets[0])
                    s.offered_trade_keys.update(self.trade_keys(sent_sheets))
                    price = self.their_price(s, m["term_sheets"][0]["terms"])
                    s.ours.append(price)
                    s.gaps.append(max(0.0, (theirs - price) / theirs) if theirs else 0.0)
            else:
                sheets = m.get("term_sheets") or []
                if sheets and sheets[0].get("terms", {}).get("unit_price") is not None:
                    theirs = self.their_price(s, sheets[0]["terms"])
                    if s.ours:
                        s.theirs.append(theirs)
        if events and events[-1].get("from") != "buyer" and s.theirs:
            s.theirs.pop()  # the latest reply is read by move() like any fresh reply
        self.note(sid, "restore", ours=s.ours, theirs=s.theirs, terms=s.terms)

    # -- reading its reply -------------------------------------------------------------------
    def read_signals(self, s, body):
        """Persona traits in its own e-mail (a supplier the package does not know, or news since):
        merged into the profile; a cash need raises what money now is worth to it."""
        new = [k for k in signals_in(body) if k not in s.prof["signals"]]
        if not new:
            return
        s.prof["signals"] = sorted(s.prof["signals"] + new)
        if "cash_need" in new:
            s.prof["rate"] = round(s.prof["rate"] + 0.05, 3)
            if s.est:
                s.est["interest_rate"] = s.prof["rate"]
        self.note(s.sid, "signals", new=new)

    def bound_full_cost(self, s, terms):
        """A supplier does not offer below its cost floor (`docs/api.md`, What counts): every sheet
        it sends, valued to it (its clause included), bounds our full-cost estimate from above. The
        should-cost overshot the true full cost by 1 to 2 % on P01, P02 and P03 (the relationship
        charge of 32 practice deals), and the relationship target built on it closed above the
        supplier's own counter (P01: 131.27 in 8 sessions, 0.909, against 130.08, 0.978)."""
        full_cost = s.est.get("full_cost")
        if not full_cost:
            return
        offered = eco.value(self.case, terms, s.est)
        if offered < full_cost:
            s.est["full_cost"] = offered
            self.note(s.sid, "full_cost_bound", offered=round(offered, 2), was=round(full_cost, 2))

    def listen(self, s, body):
        """The live analyst on its latest e-mail: the mood goes to the writer, the tactic paces our
        next price and our evidence, the argument it recognised picks our prepared answer, its
        asks join what the patterns found. Its time comes out of the writer's; late or off, the
        move goes on with the patterns alone."""
        s.mood, s.tactic, s.argument = None, None, 0
        if self.writer_s < ANALYST_MIN_S:  # several threads share the clocks: the move comes first
            return
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        arguments = s.playbook.get("arguments") or []
        seen = analyst.read(self.complete, self.case, body, s.ours, s.theirs, arguments, self.writer_s / 2)
        self.writer_s -= time.monotonic() - t0
        if seen is None:
            return
        s.asks = [k for k in ASKS if k in s.asks or k in seen["asks"]]
        s.mood, s.tactic, s.argument, s.live = seen["mood"], seen["tactic"], seen["argument"], seen["notes"]
        s.tactics.append(s.tactic)
        self.note(s.sid, "analyst", seconds=round(time.monotonic() - t0, 1), **seen)

    def team_facts(self, s, first, extra):
        """What the team adds to the writer's facts: our prepared answer to the argument its e-mail
        made, a weak point to press in the opening, the trades on offer, the mood to meet."""
        out = []
        rebuttals = s.playbook.get("rebuttals") or []
        if s.argument and s.argument <= len(rebuttals) and rebuttals[s.argument - 1]:
            out.append(
                f'they argue: "{s.playbook["arguments"][s.argument - 1]}" Our answer, in your own words: '
                f"{rebuttals[s.argument - 1]}"
            )
        if first and s.playbook.get("press"):
            out.append(f"a point to raise politely, once: {s.playbook['press'][0]}")
        if extra:
            why = "; ".join(t["why"] for t in [*s.trades, *s.active_trades] if t.get("why"))
            out.append(
                "our proposal lists alternative packages after the first one: say they are free to choose the "
                f"one that suits them best ({why})"
            )
        elif s.active_trades:
            why = "; ".join(t["why"] for t in s.active_trades if t.get("why"))
            out.append(f"we adjusted the package in response to {why}; explain the commercial terms clearly")
        if s.mood == "irritated":
            out.append("they sound irritated: acknowledge it sincerely before anything else")
        elif s.mood == "pressured":
            out.append("they sound under pressure: be calm and make the next step easy for them")
        return out

    def their_price(self, s, terms):
        """Its sheet as a price at our planned terms (same value to it)."""
        same = all(terms.get(k) == v for k, v in s.terms.items() if k != "unit_price" and k in terms)
        if same:
            return terms["unit_price"]
        v = eco.value(self.case, terms, s.est)
        return round(eco.price_for_value(self.case, s.terms, s.est, v), 2)

    def switch(self, s, new, why):
        """Plan new non-price terms; our last price moves to the same value for the supplier."""
        if s.ours:
            v = eco.value(self.case, eco.at_price(s.terms, s.ours[-1]), s.est)
            s.ours[-1] = round(eco.price_for_value(self.case, new, s.est, v), 2)
        if s.theirs:
            v = eco.value(self.case, eco.at_price(s.terms, s.theirs[-1]), s.est)
            s.theirs[-1] = round(eco.price_for_value(self.case, new, s.est, v), 2)
        s.terms = {**new}
        self.note(s.sid, "switch_terms", why=why, terms={k: v for k, v in new.items() if k != "unit_price"})

    def adopt(self, s, sheets):
        """Compare complete quoted packages, then switch once to the cheapest useful one."""
        if not s.ours:
            return
        case = self.case
        standing = sheets[0]["terms"]
        planned_cost = eco.cost(case, eco.at_price(s.terms, self.their_price(s, standing)), s.std, s.est)
        candidates = []
        for sheet in sheets:
            new = eco.quoted_offer(case, sheet["terms"], s.std)
            if new is None or all(new.get(k) == v for k, v in s.terms.items() if k != "unit_price"):
                continue
            c = eco.deal_cost(case, new, s.std, s.est)
            if c is not None and c < planned_cost - max(1.0, 0.001 * planned_cost):
                candidates.append((c, new))
        if candidates:
            _, new = min(candidates, key=lambda row: (row[0], repr(sorted(row[1].items()))))
            self.switch(s, new, "complete quoted package costs us less")

    # -- one move ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def move(self, sid, threads, writer_s=llm.TIMEOUT_S):
        """The next message to this supplier: {"message": ...}, or None when the thread is done.
        `writer_s`: what the supplier clocks leave for the model paragraph."""
        s, events = self.sides[sid], threads[sid]
        self.writer_s = writer_s
        s.prev_state = s.state
        last = latest(events)
        status = last.get("status")
        if s.state == "ended" or status in ENDED:
            s.state = "ended"
            return None
        sheets = [sh for sh in last.get("term_sheets") or [] if sh.get("terms", {}).get("unit_price") is not None]
        if not sheets:
            s.state = "ended" if not standing(events)[0] else "done"
            return None
        std_before = s.std
        s.std = standard_terms(events) or s.std
        fresh = s.last_reply is not last
        if fresh:
            terms_before = dict(s.terms)
            estimate_before = dict(s.est)
            self.adopt(s, sheets)
            s.term_change = any(sheets[0]["terms"].get(k, v) != v for k, v in terms_before.items() if k != "unit_price")
            s.theirs.append(self.their_price(s, sheets[0]["terms"]))
            self.bound_full_cost(s, sheets[0]["terms"])
            s.last_sheet = sheets[0]["terms"]
            s.last_reply = last
            s.asks = asks(last.get("body"))
            self.read_signals(s, last.get("body"))
            if self.briefs is not None and status not in DONE:
                self.listen(s, last.get("body"))
            economics_changed = s.terms != terms_before or s.est != estimate_before or s.std != std_before
            if s.target is not None and economics_changed:
                s.target = eco.relationship_optimum(
                    self.case,
                    s.terms,
                    s.std,
                    s.est,
                    s.est["full_cost"] * 0.85,
                    max(s.est["full_cost"] * 0.85, s.quote, s.target, s.theirs[-1]),
                )
        theirs = s.theirs[-1]
        if s.state == "mirror":  # we sent its own sheet: done
            s.state = "done"
            return None
        left = self.moves_left(s, events)
        if status in DONE or left <= 0:
            return self.finish(s, sheets, events, theirs, left)
        cap = eco.break_even(self.case, s.terms, s.std, s.est)
        if s.ours and s.target and theirs <= s.target:
            # The supplier already offers at or below our estimated optimum. Let the close gate
            # evaluate its standing sheet instead of raising the price to our target.
            s.state = "done"
            return None
        if s.ours and theirs <= s.ours[-1]:  # it came below what we offered: take it
            return self.finish(s, sheets, events, theirs, left)
        price, n_claims = self.next_price(s, theirs)
        if cap is not None and price > cap:
            price = max(cap, s.ours[-1]) if s.ours else cap  # never above the alternative, never back down
            self.note(sid, "break_even_cap", cap=cap, price=price)
        claims = self.pick(s, n_claims, threads)
        sheets = [eco.at_price(s.terms, price)]
        if not s.ours and s.trades:
            sheets += safe(lambda: self.trade_sheets(s, sheets[0]), [])[:2]
        elif s.ours:
            sheets += safe(lambda: self.need_trade_sheets(s, sheets[0]), [])[:2]
        switched_trade_keys = set()
        if self.same_offer(s.last_sent_terms, sheets[0]):
            if len(sheets) == 1:
                s.state = "done"
                self.note(sid, "no_progress", reason="unchanged price and terms")
                return None
            # Do not resend the old primary sheet. Move the thread onto the best new package,
            # whose buyer cost is lower and whose estimated supplier value matches the main offer.
            switched_trade_keys = self.trade_keys(sheets)
            sheet = sheets[1]
            old_target = s.target

def rows(pkg, sql, params=(), limit=8):

def block(title, data):
    data = [d for d in data if d]
    if not data:
        return ""
    return f"{title}:\n" + "\n".join(d if isinstance(d, str) else json.dumps(d, ensure_ascii=False) for d in data)


def case_brief(case):
    """The case as every subagent sees it."""
    b = case["buyer"]

    return block(
        "CASE",
        [
            f"{case.get('title')} ({case.get('type')})",
            case.get("briefing"),
            {k: b.get(k) for k in keep},
            {"negotiable": case.get("negotiable"), "term_options": case.get("term_options")},
        ],
    )

def index_moves(pkg, part):
    """The part's cost drivers with each index's change over the last 12 months."""
    out = []
    for d in rows(pkg, "SELECT series_id, weight FROM cost_drivers WHERE part_id = ?", (part,)):
        sql = "SELECT value FROM index_values WHERE series_id = ? ORDER BY month DESC"
        v = rows(pkg, sql, (d["series_id"],), 13)
        if len(v) == 13 and v[12]["value"]:
            d["change_12m_pct"] = round((v[0]["value"] / v[12]["value"] - 1) * 100, 1)
        out.append(d)
    return out

exports/README.md # Exports: the Saturday probe sessions as tables

Every session we played on Saturday 10 October: 15 practice sessions (all 10 hosted cases) and 17
sandbox sessions, joined with the case files and the data package. What we learned from them is
in `docs/learnings.md`. Money is EUR over the case horizon; C is the arena's total cost
(`arena_kit.total_cost`), lower is better. This is a snapshot: the probe and the script that built
it (`buyer/autoprobe.py`, `analysis/export.py`) are in the closed PR #5, commit `03c51bc`.

| File | One row per | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| `sessions.csv`, `.jsonl` | session | outcomes: score, C open/deal/alt/best, deal terms, cost breakdown |
| `threads.csv`, `.jsonl` | supplier in a session | supplier profile from the data next to what it did |
| `messages.jsonl` | e-mail, both directions | the full negotiation: terms with C, status, claims, reasons, back office |
| `claims.csv` | data argument we made | which arguments the arena verified, and for whom |

Join keys: `session_id` (+ `supplier_id`, + `round`). `set` is `practice` or `sandbox`.

## How we played

`method` in `sessions`:

- `autoprobe v1`: a fixed experiment per supplier thread, then the cheapest valid close. Its steps
  are `probe_step` in `messages` and `probe_steps` in `threads`:
  - `open`: questions and documents (cost breakdown, delivery schedule or 8D), our anchor price
  - `ours`: up to 3 sheets at the supplier's price, each with one lever moved our way
  - `theirs`: up to 3 sheets a step below, each with one lever moved its way
  - `claims`: up to 3 verified data arguments with a concession
  - `step`: concessions until `final_offer` or `agreed`; `push`: one ask after `agreed`
  - `keepalive`: a short question so a waiting RFQ thread does not time out
- `scripted probe (resumed by hand)`: an earlier version of the same steps (P01, first P10 run).
- `sandbox A/B: <variant>`: D01 with identical sheets, round 3 varied (`baseline`, `bluff`,
  `urgency`).
- `kit naive agent`: the kit's `NaiveAgent`.

## sessions

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `score` | `(c_open - c_deal) / (c_open - c_best)`, clipped 0..1; no deal scores the alternative |
| `c_open`, `c_deal`, `c_alt`, `c_best` | C of the best opening quote, our deal, our alternative, the best package any supplier would accept (hidden floor, revealed after the session) |
| `gap_to_best_eur` | `c_deal - c_best`: money left on the table |
| `implied_price_at_deal_terms` | the unit price at which our deal's other terms would cost exactly `c_best`; it keeps the deal's coverage, so for an under-covered deal (P08, P18) it mixes coverage and price |
| `deal_*` | the closed terms (unstated fields filled with the supplier's standard terms) |
| `cost_*` | `c_deal` by part: price, uncovered_need, fallback_risk, payment_terms, freight, late_delivery, quality, tooling, index_clause, index_risk, relationship |

## threads

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `country`, `owner_type`, `credit_index`, `scorecard_colour`, `data_signals` | from the data package (`analysis/explore.py`, `analysis/out/profiles.csv`); signals are persona traits found in notes, letters and news, e.g. `cash_need`, `price_frozen`, `capacity_full` |
| `should_cost` | the package's `should_cost` table, the supplier's own plant if modelled |
| `opening_price`, `final_price`, `price_move_pct` | its first and last unit price in the thread |
| `opening_vs_should_cost_pct` | how far its quote sits above (+) or below (-) the should-cost |
| `final_status`, `first_agreed_round` | `open`, `agreed`, `final_offer`, `walked_away`; the round it first said `agreed` |
| `documents`, `sent_cost_breakdown` | attachments it sent |
| `probe_steps` | our experiment sequence (see above) |
| `questions`, `backoffice_calls` | its recurring questions; its internal decisions ("My call: counter / hold / accept") |

## messages

Fields: `round`, `actor` (`buyer` / `supplier`), `probe_step` and `probe_note` (what our message
tested), `action` (`accept` / `walk_away`), `status`, `sheets` (`[{terms, c}]`: our term sheets, or
its standing sheet), `claims_made` (typed as the arena read them), `claim_results`, `missing_fields`,
`signals` (reply delay, validity), `reasons` (the supplier's reasons in words, hidden figures as `…`),
`backoffice` (its roles talking internally that round), `text` (the e-mail).

## claims

`type` (`index_change`, `quality_record`, `delivery_record`, `should_cost`, `volume_change`,
`notice`, ...), `refs` (data IDs), `asserted` (our figure as the arena parsed it), `result`
(`verified`, `contradicted`, `duplicate`, `irrelevant`).

exports/README.md # Exports: the Saturday probe sessions as tables

Every session we played on Saturday 10 October: 15 practice sessions (all 10 hosted cases) and 17
sandbox sessions, joined with the case files and the data package. What we learned from them is
in `docs/learnings.md`. Money is EUR over the case horizon; C is the arena's total cost
(`arena_kit.total_cost`), lower is better. This is a snapshot: the probe and the script that built
it (`buyer/autoprobe.py`, `analysis/export.py`) are in the closed PR #5, commit `03c51bc`.

| File | One row per | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| `sessions.csv`, `.jsonl` | session | outcomes: score, C open/deal/alt/best, deal terms, cost breakdown |
| `threads.csv`, `.jsonl` | supplier in a session | supplier profile from the data next to what it did |
| `messages.jsonl` | e-mail, both directions | the full negotiation: terms with C, status, claims, reasons, back office |
| `claims.csv` | data argument we made | which arguments the arena verified, and for whom |

Join keys: `session_id` (+ `supplier_id`, + `round`). `set` is `practice` or `sandbox`.

## How we played

`method` in `sessions`:

- `autoprobe v1`: a fixed experiment per supplier thread, then the cheapest valid close. Its steps
  are `probe_step` in `messages` and `probe_steps` in `threads`:
  - `open`: questions and documents (cost breakdown, delivery schedule or 8D), our anchor price
  - `ours`: up to 3 sheets at the supplier's price, each with one lever moved our way
  - `theirs`: up to 3 sheets a step below, each with one lever moved its way
  - `claims`: up to 3 verified data arguments with a concession
  - `step`: concessions until `final_offer` or `agreed`; `push`: one ask after `agreed`
  - `keepalive`: a short question so a waiting RFQ thread does not time out
- `scripted probe (resumed by hand)`: an earlier version of the same steps (P01, first P10 run).
- `sandbox A/B: <variant>`: D01 with identical sheets, round 3 varied (`baseline`, `bluff`,
  `urgency`).
- `kit naive agent`: the kit's `NaiveAgent`.

## sessions

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `score` | `(c_open - c_deal) / (c_open - c_best)`, clipped 0..1; no deal scores the alternative |
| `c_open`, `c_deal`, `c_alt`, `c_best` | C of the best opening quote, our deal, our alternative, the best package any supplier would accept (hidden floor, revealed after the session) |
| `gap_to_best_eur` | `c_deal - c_best`: money left on the table |
| `implied_price_at_deal_terms` | the unit price at which our deal's other terms would cost exactly `c_best`; it keeps the deal's coverage, so for an under-covered deal (P08, P18) it mixes coverage and price |
| `deal_*` | the closed terms (unstated fields filled with the supplier's standard terms) |
| `cost_*` | `c_deal` by part: price, uncovered_need, fallback_risk, payment_terms, freight, late_delivery, quality, tooling, index_clause, index_risk, relationship |

## threads

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `country`, `owner_type`, `credit_index`, `scorecard_colour`, `data_signals` | from the data package (`analysis/explore.py`, `analysis/out/profiles.csv`); signals are persona traits found in notes, letters and news, e.g. `cash_need`, `price_frozen`, `capacity_full` |
| `should_cost` | the package's `should_cost` table, the supplier's own plant if modelled |
| `opening_price`, `final_price`, `price_move_pct` | its first and last unit price in the thread |
| `opening_vs_should_cost_pct` | how far its quote sits above (+) or below (-) the should-cost |
| `final_status`, `first_agreed_round` | `open`, `agreed`, `final_offer`, `walked_away`; the round it first said `agreed` |
| `documents`, `sent_cost_breakdown` | attachments it sent |
| `probe_steps` | our experiment sequence (see above) |
| `questions`, `backoffice_calls` | its recurring questions; its internal decisions ("My call: counter / hold / accept") |

## messages

Fields: `round`, `actor` (`buyer` / `supplier`), `probe_step` and `probe_note` (what our message
tested), `action` (`accept` / `walk_away`), `status`, `sheets` (`[{terms, c}]`: our term sheets, or
its standing sheet), `claims_made` (typed as the arena read them), `claim_results`, `missing_fields`,
`signals` (reply delay, validity), `reasons` (the supplier's reasons in words, hidden figures as `…`),
`backoffice` (its roles talking internally that round), `text` (the e-mail).

## claims

`type` (`index_change`, `quality_record`, `delivery_record`, `should_cost`, `volume_change`,
`notice`, ...), `refs` (data IDs), `asserted` (our figure as the arena parsed it), `result`
(`verified`, `contradicted`, `duplicate`, `irrelevant`).

(result, trace with the supplier's reasons, back office) into logs/ for the learning loop."""

import argparse
import functools
import json
import logging
import os
import statistics
from pathlib import Path

from arena_kit import ArenaClient, ArenaError, RemoteTable, play, play_all
from arena_kit.agents import NaiveAgent
from arena_kit.cli import load_env, summary
from arena_kit.data import DataPackage
from arena_kit.play import hosted, play_waves

from . import llm, runner

LOGS = Path("logs/sessions")
AGENTS = ("buyer", "naive")  # our policy (`policy.py`, played by `runner.py`) or the kit's baseline


def load_package(path):
    """The data package with its ID index built once, before parallel cases share it."""
    if not path:
        return None
    pkg = DataPackage(path)
    pkg.lookup("")
    return pkg


def pull(client, set_):
    """Save every ended session of a set that has its trace to logs/sessions/<set>/, once."""
    out = LOGS / set_
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    saved = 0
    for s in client.sessions(set_):
        path = out / f"{s['case_id'].split(':')[-1]}_{s['session_id']}.json"
        if s["status"] != "ended" or path.exists():
            continue
        state = client.session(s["session_id"])
        if not (state.get("result") or {}).get("trace"):  # final: the trace comes after the final
            continue
        try:
            state["backoffice"] = client.backoffice(s["session_id"])
        except ArenaError:
            state["backoffice"] = None
        path.write_text(json.dumps(state, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
        saved += 1
    print(f"{saved} new sessions in {out}")


def case_file(client, case_id):
    """The case file before its session opens (free, no quota), for the research team; None when
    the arena does not list it."""
    for set_ in ("sandbox", "practice"):
        for case in client.cases(set_):
            if case["case_id"] == case_id:
                return case
    return None


def main(argv=None):
    load_env()
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="buyer")
    ap.add_argument("-v", "--verbose", action="store_true")
    verbose = argparse.ArgumentParser(add_help=False)  # -v also after the command
    verbose.add_argument("-v", "--verbose", action="store_true", default=argparse.SUPPRESS)
    verbose.add_argument("--no-llm", action="store_true", default=argparse.SUPPRESS, help="template e-mails only")
    verbose.add_argument(
        "--no-team",
        action="store_true",
        default=argparse.SUPPRESS,
        help="the plain price engine: no research team, no live analyst, no debrief",
    )
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    sub.add_parser = functools.partial(sub.add_parser, parents=[verbose])
    data = {"default": os.environ.get("ARENA_DATA"), "help": "data package folder"}
    p = sub.add_parser("play", help="play one case")
    p.add_argument("case_id")
    p.add_argument("--agent", default="buyer", choices=AGENTS)
    p.add_argument("--data", **data)
    r = sub.add_parser("run", help="play every playable case of a set in parallel; final: wave by wave")
    r.add_argument("--set", default="practice", choices=["practice", "sandbox", "final"])
    r.add_argument("--agent", default="buyer", choices=AGENTS)
    r.add_argument("--data", **data)
    r.add_argument("--parallel", type=int, default=8, help="cases at once (at most 10)")
    r.add_argument("--waves", type=int, default=5, help="final: stop after this many waves have closed")
    r.add_argument("--cases", help="practice or sandbox: only these cases, e.g. P01,P08")
    s = sub.add_parser("pull", help="save finished sessions with trace and back office to logs/sessions/")
    s.add_argument("--set", default="practice", choices=["practice", "sandbox", "final"])
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    args.no_llm = getattr(args, "no_llm", False)
    team = not getattr(args, "no_team", False)
    logging.basicConfig(
        level=logging.INFO if args.verbose else logging.WARNING,
        format="%(asctime)s %(message)s",
        datefmt="%H:%M:%S",
    )
    client = ArenaClient()

    if args.cmd == "pull":
        return pull(client, args.set)
    naive = args.agent == "naive"
    pkg = None if naive else load_package(args.data)
    complete = None if naive or args.no_llm else llm.complete_from_env()
    if args.cmd == "play":
        try:
            if naive:
                table = RemoteTable(client)
                result = play(table, args.case_id, NaiveAgent())
            else:
                table = runner.PracticeTable(client, case_file(client, args.case_id))
                result = runner.play_case(table, args.case_id, pkg, complete=complete, team=team)
        except ArenaError as e:  # e.g. not hosted, the quota, a paused key: the arena says why
            raise SystemExit(str(e)) from None
        print(json.dumps(summary(result), indent=2))
        state = client.session(table.session_id)
        print(f"replay: {os.environ['ARENA_URL'].rstrip('/')}{state.get('replay_url')}")
        pull(client, state["set"])
    elif args.set == "final":  # no human in the loop: waits for each wave, plays it within its cap
        parallel = min(args.parallel, 10)
        if naive:
            out = play_waves(client, NaiveAgent, args.waves, parallel)
        else:
            out = runner.play_waves(client, pkg, args.waves, parallel, complete=complete, team=team)
        for case_id, result in out.items():
            print(case_id, result if isinstance(result, Exception) else summary(result))
    else:

class ArenaClient:
    def __init__(
        self,
        base_url=None,
        api_key=None,
        *,
        retries=3,
        transport=None,
        timeout=TIMEOUT_S,
        rate=CALLS_PER_SECOND,
    ):
        base_url = (base_url or os.environ.get("ARENA_URL", "")).rstrip("/")
        if not base_url:
            raise ValueError("set ARENA_URL (e.g. https://…) or pass base_url")
        key = api_key or os.environ.get("ARENA_API_KEY")
        headers = {"X-API-Key": key} if key else {}
        self.retries, self.rate, self._lock, self._next = retries, rate, threading.Lock(), 0.0
        self.practice_remaining = None  # from the last practice reply that said so
        self.http = httpx.Client(base_url=f"{base_url}/v1", headers=headers, timeout=timeout, transport=transport)

    def _pace(self):
        with self._lock:
            now = time.monotonic()
            wait, self._next = self._next - now, max(now, self._next) + 1 / self.rate
        if wait > 0:
            time.sleep(wait)

"""What the team learned, case after case: after a case closes, a debrief subagent reads how it
went and writes one lesson; the lead researcher reads what we did in similar cases and what came
of it before the next one (the figures, not the lesson: one run is a data point). Rows are keyed on
features (goal, case type, owner type, traits), never on a case or supplier ID, and code writes
every figure in them."""

import json
import logging
import threading
from pathlib import Path

from . import llm

log = logging.getLogger("buyer")
LESSONS = Path(__file__).parent / "lessons.jsonl"  # committed: the final machine starts with them
RECALL = 5
LOCK = threading.Lock()

DEBRIEF = """You are the debrief analyst of the purchasing team of Hollerau Pumpenwerke. Below is how
one negotiation went, in shares of the supplier's quote: where we opened, our price path, its
price path, its reasons in its own words, and the score (1.0 is the best deal that was possible,
0 is no better than its first offer).
Our team can change four things only: which terms it offers as a trade next to its main proposal,
which kind of argument it cites first, how it answers the supplier's arguments, and its tone.
Code sets the prices and the pace. Threats, deadlines, bluffs and requests for cost data have been tested and
do not work, never suggest them.
Write the one lesson for the next negotiation with this KIND of supplier (owner type, traits,
goal): what its path and reasons show about how it concedes and when it stops, and which of the
four things to do differently, or to keep if the score is high.
Never name the supplier, the part, the case or any ID, and give no absolute prices.
Return JSON only: {"lesson": "one or two short sentences"}"""


def features(case, sides):
    return {
        "goal": case["buyer"].get("category_goal"),
        "type": case.get("type"),
        "bidders": len(sides),
        "owners": sorted({s.prof.get("owner_type") or "unknown" for s in sides}),
        "signals": sorted({k for s in sides for k in s.prof.get("signals", [])}),
    }


def path(side):
    """A thread in shares of its quote: what the debrief and the next lead can compare."""
    q = side.quote or 1.0
    return {
        "opened": round(side.ours[0] / q, 3),
        "ours": [round(p / q, 3) for p in side.ours],
        "theirs": [round(p / q, 3) for p in side.theirs],
        "tactics": side.tactics,
        "trades": [f"{t['field']}={t['value']}" for t in side.trades],
    }


def reasons(result, sid):
    """Its reasons round by round, from the replay (practice and sandbox)."""
    out = []
    for step in result.get("trace") or []:
        if step.get("actor") == sid and step.get("reasons"):
            out.append(f"round {step.get('round')}: " + " ".join(str(r) for r in step["reasons"])[:400])
    return out


def record(case, neg, result, complete):
    """Append this case's lesson. Only a case with a score teaches (the final shows none)."""
    if result.get("score") is None:
        return None
    sides = [s for s in neg.sides.values() if s.ours]
    if not sides:
        return None
    won = neg.sides.get(result.get("supplier_id"))
    row = {
        **features(case, sides),
        "deal": bool(result.get("deal")),
        "score": round(result["score"], 3),
        "threads": [path(s) for s in ([won] if won and won.ours else sides)],
    }
    user = json.dumps({**row, "reasons": [r for s in sides for r in reasons(result, s.sid)][-12:]}, ensure_ascii=False)
    answer = llm.ask_json(complete, DEBRIEF, user) or {}
    row["lesson"] = " ".join(str(answer.get("lesson") or "").split())[:300]
    with LOCK, LESSONS.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps(row, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
    return row


def recall(case, n=RECALL):
    """The latest runs of the most similar cases (same goal, then same case type), as lines: what
    we did and what came of it. The debrief's lesson stays in the file: it is one run's story, and
    the lead would read it as a rule."""
    if not LESSONS.is_file():
        return []
    rows = []
    for line in LESSONS.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        try:
            rows.append(json.loads(line))
        except ValueError:
            continue
    goal, kind = case["buyer"].get("category_goal"), case.get("type")
    ranked = sorted(enumerate(rows), key=lambda r: ((r[1].get("goal") == goal) + (r[1].get("type") == kind), r[0]))
    out = []
    for _, r in ranked[-n:]:
        if r.get("goal") != goal and r.get("type") != kind:
            continue
        t = (r.get("threads") or [{}])[0]
        out.append(
            f"{r.get('goal')} {r.get('type')}, {r.get('bidders')} bidder(s), owner {'/'.join(r.get('owners') or [])}, "
            f"traits {r.get('signals')}: opened at {t.get('opened')} of the quote, offered trades "
            f"{t.get('trades') or []}, its prices {t.get('theirs')}, score {r.get('score')}."
        )
    return out

    with LOCK, LESSONS.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps(row, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
    return row


def recall(case, n=RECALL):
    """The latest runs of the most similar cases (same goal, then same case type), as lines: what
    we did and what came of it. The debrief's lesson stays in the file: it is one run's story, and
    the lead would read it as a rule."""
    if not LESSONS.is_file():
        return []
    rows = []
    for line in LESSONS.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        try:
            rows.append(json.loads(line))
        except ValueError:
            continue
    goal, kind = case["buyer"].get("category_goal"), case.get("type")
    ranked = sorted(enumerate(rows), key=lambda r: ((r[1].get("goal") == goal) + (r[1].get("type") == kind), r[0]))
    out = []
    for _, r in ranked[-n:]:
        if r.get("goal") != goal and r.get("type") != kind:
            continue
        t = (r.get("threads") or [{}])[0]
        out.append(
            f"{r.get('goal')} {r.get('type')}, {r.get('bidders')} bidder(s), owner {'/'.join(r.get('owners') or [])}, "
            f"traits {r.get('signals')}: opened at {t.get('opened')} of the quote, offered trades "
            f"{t.get('trades') or []}, its prices {t.get('theirs')}, score {r.get('score')}."
        )
    return out
"}

**Codacabana is an autonomous procurement buyer that researches suppliers, negotiates by email, and evaluates the full economic value of a contract before accepting it.** The strongest pitch story is: **we evolved from scripted negotiation and regex-based interpretation into an agentic procurement team, while keeping financial decisions under deterministic control.** The logs show substantial progress, although they do not yet establish that adding agents outperforms the mature rules engine. **What the project does** Built for Hollerau Pumpenwerke in the Tacto Negotiation Arena, the buyer: - Studies supplier profiles, contracts, purchase history, forecasts, quality records, and cost indices. - Negotiates prices alongside payment, delivery, volume, duration, quality, and indexation. - Coordinates competing suppliers and uses their actual offers as negotiation evidence. - Accepts a valid standing offer when its total cost beats the alternative, or walks away. The company dataset contains **447 suppliers, 46 detailed supplier profiles, and 60 parts**. The business problem is that a cheaper unit price can still produce a more expensive contract through quality failures, financing, uncovered demand, or supplier relationship costs. **The evolution, supported by the logs** | Stage | What changed | Recorded result | |---|---|---| | **1. Scripted exploration** | Fixed sequences tested anchors, questions, term changes, and evidence. These runs helped reveal supplier behavior. | Initial export: **15 practice sessions, 0.2465 mean score**, 14 deals. This includes repeated cases and some manually resumed exploration. | | **2. Rules and regex engine** | Supplier traits and requests were recognized through text patterns. Code selected packages, prices, concessions, and closing actions. An optional LLM wrote an email paragraph. | Complete `practice-v5` batch: **0.7033**, **10/10 deals**. | | **3. Better economics and evidence** | Added clause trades, falling-index arguments, relationship-aware pricing, preservation of quoted packages, and closing fixes. | A later complete ten-case validation: **0.7838**, **10/10 deals**. | | **4. Agentic research and negotiation** | Added specialist researchers, strategy synthesis, simulated buyer/supplier rehearsal, and a live analyst that interprets replies and advises tactics. | Documented team batch: **0.7772**, **10/10 deals**. A context experiment scored **0.7604**, also 10/10. | | **5. Agentic refinement** | Tested richer session evidence and repaired proposal-generation failures. | Repaired candidate: **0.7808**, **10/10 valid deals**. Its report records **not promoted**. | Sources: [initial exports](https://github.com/stegra05/ehl-codacabana-final/blob/0fef4eebd26779f89cae02ce0bcf5b29fc2e157d/exports/README.md), [v5 log](https://github.com/stegra05/ehl-codacabana-final/blob/0fef4eebd26779f89cae02ce0bcf5b29fc2e157d/logs/practice-v5.log), [validation results](/Users/joaofmzuffo/ehl-codacabana-final/out/pr18-hosted-practice/20261010-225933/results.json), [team results](https://github.com/stegra05/ehl-codacabana-final/blob/0fef4eebd26779f89cae02ce0bcf5b29fc2e157d/docs/learnings.md), [repaired candidate](/Users/joaofmzuffo/ehl-codacabana-final/out/session-evidence-practice/20261011-064407/final-report.json). For the results slide, use **“0.70 → 0.78 across complete ten-case validations.”** Show the initial exploration separately because its case mix differs. The repository’s shorthand “0.32 → 0.66 → 0.73” lacks sufficiently clear batch definitions for a clean comparison. A useful engineering lesson: an earlier agentic evidence run scored **0.5257 with 7/10 deals**, following zero-price API errors and timeouts. Also, two evidence experiments averaged **0.7808 versus the preceding 0.7838 baseline**, so they were not promoted. Progress came through testing and rejecting regressions. **The business result to put on the slide** The **0.7838 ten-case validation** produced: | Metric | Result | |---|---:| | Deals closed | **10/10** | | Opening total contract cost | **€12.760 million** | | Negotiated total contract cost | **€11.571 million** | | Reduction versus opening offers | **€1.189 million / 9.32%** | These are **simulated contract economics across the benchmark case horizons**, not realized customer savings. An Arena score of 0.7838 is a normalized benchmark score, not a 78.38% price reduction. [Calculation evidence](/Users/joaofmzuffo/ehl-codacabana-final/out/pitch-evidence/summary.json). **The architecture today** ```mermaid flowchart TD D["Company data
Contracts, orders, forecasts, indices, supplier records"] R["Four research specialists
Economics · Persona · History · Leverage"] L["Lead researcher
Trade ideas, evidence priorities, tone"] H["Buyer and supplier rehearsal
Expected arguments and responses"] S["Supplier email and structured offer"] A["Live analyst
Requests, mood, argument, tactic"] P["Negotiation policy and supplier state"] E["Economic engine
Total cost, allowed terms, must-haves"] W["Writer
Approved figures, cited evidence, model paragraph"] O["Runner and Arena API
Scheduling, deadlines, send and recovery"] C["Closing gate
Valid standing offer below alternative cost"] M["Practice logs and memory"] D --> R --> L --> H --> P S --> A --> P P <--> E P --> W --> O --> S P --> C --> O O --> M M --> L ``` The responsibilities are deliberately separated: - **Research team:** four specialist model roles study different evidence; a lead researcher proposes trades and argument priorities. - **Rehearsal:** supplier and buyer roles anticipate objections and prepare responses. This is a planning simulation. - **Live analyst:** interprets each reply and selects constrained advice such as `steady`, `hold`, or `argue`. That advice can affect concession pacing and wording. - **Policy and economics:** calculate prices, value full packages using `arena_kit.total_cost`, validate constraints, and decide whether to accept. - **Writer:** combines exact code-selected terms and cited claims with model-written prose. - **Runner:** manages supplier clocks, parallel cases, API recovery, and closing before deadlines. - **Memory:** records practice outcomes for later preparation. The final runner disables new lesson recording. **Regex remains in the system**, particularly for supplier traits and request detection. The evolution is an agentic layer around an established economic engine, rather than a complete replacement. I checked this against `main` at **`0fef4ee`**. The architecture document still describes the earlier paragraph-only model role; the current [research](https://github.com/stegra05/ehl-codacabana-final/blob/0fef4eebd26779f89cae02ce0bcf5b29fc2e157d/buyer/research.py), [analyst](https://github.com/stegra05/ehl-codacabana-final/blob/0fef4eebd26779f89cae02ce0bcf5b29fc2e157d/buyer/analyst.py), and [policy](https://github.com/stegra05/ehl-codacabana-final/blob/0fef4eebd26779f89cae02ce0bcf5b29fc2e157d/buyer/policy.py) code establish the newer architecture. **Suggested pitch narrative** > “Procurement decisions depend on much more than price. Our buyer brings together supplier research, contract economics, and autonomous negotiation. > > We started with scripted experiments and regex rules to understand the environment. We then built an economic engine that evaluates complete contracts. Finally, we added a team of research and negotiation agents that interprets supplier context and adapts its arguments. > > In one complete ten-case validation, we closed every deal and reduced simulated total contract cost by €1.19 million, or 9.3%, versus opening offers. Our design gives language models room to interpret and negotiate while code controls the financial commitments.” Build the presentation around five slides: **problem → autonomous workflow → architecture → measured evolution → one negotiation example**. The refreshed practice catalog contains **468 completed sessions and 440 deals across all historical policies**. Use that as evidence of experimentation, not as the success rate of the current version. No final results were accessed.
